question.question:
A retailer reports operating cash flows using the direct method. For the year, cost of goods sold is 610000 USD and includes no write-downs; every inventory purchase is made on credit from trade suppliers, and trade payables arise solely from those suppliers. Opening inventory is 126000 USD and closing inventory is 63000 USD. Opening trade payables are 116000 USD and closing trade payables are 149000 USD. Supplier advances (cash prepaid to suppliers and later applied against purchases) are 4000 USD at the start and 11500 USD at the end; cash paid as advances is treated as cash paid to suppliers. In the year, trade payables of 54000 USD were settled by issuing the retailer's own shares, cutting payables with no cash involved. Net supplier working capital is defined as inventory plus supplier advances less trade payables, and its change as the closing balance minus the opening balance, so a positive change indicates working capital increased and absorbed cash. Find the year's inventory purchases, the change in trade payables (closing minus opening), the signed change in net supplier working capital, and cash paid to suppliers stated as a positive outflow magnitude. If the implied cash paid is negative, regard the data as inconsistent.

Answer format: return only the exact numeric value interpreted in `usd`, using finite-decimal notation when it terminates in base 10 and an irreducible `numerator/denominator` fraction otherwise, with no unit label or additional text.

slots.description: Inventory purchases for the year derived from cost of goods sold and inventory balances
Change in trade payables, closing minus opening, signed
Signed change in net supplier working capital, positive when cash is absorbed
